editorial:
Imagine you are a high school senior with your whole life planned out, but one failed French class stands between you and your dream school, Yale. That is exactly where Bobby Chrystal finds himself. To fix things, his strict and wealthy father brings in a beautiful 29-year-old tutor to help him over the summer. The vibe here is a classic 80s mix of teenage hormones and family pressure. You get to see Bobby torn between his goofy friends, who are obsessed with losing their virginity, and his growing crush on the woman hired to teach him. It feels like a lighthearted summer romp that does not take itself too seriously.

What really works is the chemistry between the leads and the funny, awkward situations Bobby gets into. While the plot is pretty predictable, the pacing stays snappy and keeps you interested. Some parts might feel a bit dated now, but that is part of the charm. If you enjoy nostalgic coming-of-age stories with a bit of spice, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a lazy weekend movie night.
endingExplained: In the end, Bobby manages to pass his French exam thanks to the help and motivation from his tutor. This allows him to finally get into Yale and satisfy his father's high expectations. More importantly, the romantic tension between Bobby and his tutor reaches a boiling point. They move past the professional boundary, and Bobby gets the romantic experience he was chasing all summer, ending the movie on a happy and satisfying note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s teen comedies and light romance.
